title: Structured Extraction
explain: For a model that reads unstructured text (contracts, invoices, emails) and fills a fixed JSON schema, the output is checkable, so you score it against gold fields with reference-based metrics, not a judge. Layer it: schema validity as a hard gate, then per-field precision and recall after normalization, null handling, and grounding to a source span. (合法 JSON 不等于抽对了.)
model:
| Layer | How | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Schema validity | parse + schema validation | near 100% (necessary, not sufficient) |
| Field precision | reference gold | P0 fields each meet target |
| Field recall | reference gold | P0 fields each meet target |
| Exactness | normalize, then exact match | IDs, amounts, dates pass |
| Null handling | fields absent in source | hallucinated extraction under strict threshold |
| Entity linking, relations | canonical ID, relation F1 | disambiguation accuracy |
| Grounding | value traceable to a span | key values traceable |
| Robustness | noisy / OCR slice | no regression |
| Efficiency | logs | latency, tokens, cost |

**Slices:** field present, missing, duplicated, conflicting; mixed date/money/unit formats; tables, lists, OCR noise; same-name entities, pronouns; very long inputs with the field at the end.

**Scoring rules:** normalize first; report micro-F1 and macro-F1; gate critical fields separately; define list-order sensitivity.

A judge is needed only for free-text fields. Contrast [summarization](#/sd/f/eval-summarization), where no single gold string exists.

details.q: Why is schema validity not enough?
details.a: Valid JSON can hold wrong values. It is a hard gate because an unparseable output has no fields to score, but quality is field correctness. A model valid 92% of the time that is 95% right when valid has 0.92 x 0.95 = 0.874 end-to-end field accuracy, beating one that is always valid but 85% right.

details.q: Define field precision and recall, and the null case.
details.a: Precision = correct values / values emitted; recall = correct values / gold values. With 40 non-null gold fields and 10 should-be-null fields, a model that gets 36 right, 2 wrong, omits 2 and invents 4 values scores precision 36/42 = 0.86 and recall 0.90. The 4 invented values are a 0.4 hallucinated-extraction rate on the null fields.

Averaged over all fields, a few invented values are diluted. A model that fills a missing tax id with a plausible one is more dangerous than one that returns null. Make hallucinated extraction its own P0 metric, and require that values trace back to a source span.

details.q: How do you compare dates and amounts fairly?
details.a: Normalize both sides to a canonical form before exact match, and document the source convention because '03/04/2026' is ambiguous (March 4 or April 3). Fuzzy matching would also accept genuinely wrong dates.

Both. Micro is dominated by frequent fields; macro gives every field equal weight. A rare critical field (tax_id in 2% of documents versus invoice_total in 100%) needs its own precision and recall gate on top of both.

details.q: How do you handle lists and multi-valued fields?
details.a: Decide up front whether order matters. Use set-style matching with per-item F1 for order-independent lists, and penalize duplicates. Report both the item-level F1 and whether the whole list matched.

details.q: Where does a judge still belong?
details.a: Only for free-text fields (a summary of a clause, a free-form address) where exact match is wrong; use similarity or an LLM judge against the gold text, calibrated on human labels. Everything else is cheaper and more reliable as reference scoring.

prompts.q: Describe the evaluation layers for an invoice extraction product.
points: Per-field precision and recall against gold

prompts.q: How do you report scores so a rare critical field cannot hide?
points: Micro-F1 is dominated by frequent fields
Separate P0 gates per critical field
Slice by format and document type
Long-input slice with the field at the end

prompts.q: Model A is always valid but less accurate than model B, which is sometimes invalid. Which do you ship?
points: End-to-end accuracy = validity x accuracy when valid
Can invalid output be retried or repaired?
Cost of retries on latency and tokens
Compare on the critical fields, not the average
Check failure types, not just rates
